criterion_notes.c1: Examines household drinking-water supply access (piped general network vs. wells/springs and clandestine connections) and baseline household sanitation/sewerage access across six subdivisions (loteamentos) of the Águas-Lindas neighborhood in the Belém/Ananindeua metropolitan area, Pará, Brazil.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies BOTH the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading of Criterion 2. Under the plain wording, it analyzes a public water-access policy and utility governance intervention (Programa Saneamento Para Todos implemented by COSANPA under FGTS/Ministry of Cities regulations). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, rather than merely evaluating generic infrastructure delivery, the study explicitly examines rule-type mechanisms directly governing household service access, affordability, and exclusion: (1) a tariff and volumetric block-pricing rule charging R$ 24.90/month for a 10 m³ consumption cap with volumetric surcharges above 10 m³, evaluated empirically against subdivision household size and CadÚnico low-income thresholds; (2) land-occupation regularity/tenure history (formally planned/SFH-financed Verdejante vs. informal/COHAB-PA-regularized subdivisions) governing 40+ years of differential COSANPA network provision; and (3) public procurement/contractual allocation rules (Concorrência Pública nº 009/2017, five deadline extensions, opaque financial reporting, and a cap of 4,154 planned connections for 5,141 unconnected households).
criterion_notes.c3: Mixed-methods (quali-quantitative) empirical case study combining geoprocessing and quantitative tabulation of 2010 IBGE Census tract data across 6 mapped subdivisions (9,740 households; 36,362 residents), documentary audit of COSANPA's procurement contract, 5 contract amendments, and 43 monthly investment spreadsheets (2019–2022), and systematic field observation with field notes and photographic documentation in 2022.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports concrete service-access, connection, affordability, and exclusion outcomes: piped water coverage by subdivision (55.16% in formal Verdejante vs. 3.07%–15.55% in the other five subdivisions, with 67.34%–88.89% relying on wells/springs), sewerage coverage, household exceedance of the 10 m³/month tariff block (mean 3.68–3.87 residents/household vs. 3-resident limit at 110 L/person/day) and affordability burden given per-capita incomes of R$ 214.10–R$ 363.57, resident refusal of program connections / reliance on wells or clandestine connections, delayed service availability (1.19%–13.83% annual physical execution), and structural exclusion of approximately 917 unserved households not covered by the 4,154 planned connections.
criterion_notes.c5: Population and units of analysis (households, subdivisions/loteamentos, census tracts, and utility contract in Águas-Lindas, Belém/Ananindeua, PA), exposure (tariff/consumption-block rule, land-occupation regularity, and public contracting/connection allocation under Programa Saneamento Para Todos), outcome (piped connection, well reliance, affordability/block exceedance, and connection exclusion), and mixed-methods case-study design are all clearly identified. Note that systematic-review inclusion does not require a pooled quantitative effect estimate (Criterion 6 in INCLUSION_EXCLUSION.md is a meta-analysis gate only).
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Portuguese, which is directly eligible without translation under Inclusion Criterion 9.

evidence_quotes.quote: No âmbito do bairro de Águas-Lindas, o programa efetiva-se através da modalidade de abastecimento de água, sendo ofertado para a população por uma taxa de vinte e quatro reais e noventa centavos (R$ 24,90), correspondendo a uma faixa de consumo de dez metros cúbicos (10m³) de água por mês. Havendo superação desse limite, passa a incidir sobre a taxa o cálculo do consumo do beneficiário atendido pelo programa.

Parte-se de abordagem quali-quantitativa e dos seguintes procedimentos de pesquisa: a) revisão bibliográfica; b) levantamento de dados estatísticos de instituições oficiais; c) observação sistemática da paisagem, com uso do diário de campo e levantamento fotográfico; d) sistematização de dados quantitativos e produção de representações cartográficas relacionadas ao bairro.

A partir da necessidade de consumo definida pela ONU e o limite de 10m³ de água ofertado pelo programa, tem-se que apenas domicílios com até três moradores conseguiriam atender ao critério estabelecido. Assim, nos loteamentos Moara, Novas Águas Lindas e Jardim Nova Vida, que possuem as maiores médias de moradores por domicílio, o consumo de água será extrapolado, resultando diretamente no aumento da taxa originalmente ofertada.

No que se refere a formas de abastecimento de água, nota-se, apartir do quadro 03 e da figura 12, que, tanto por loteamento quanto por setor censitário, predomina abastecimento via poço ou nascente. O único loteamento que prevalece a forma de abastecimento por rede geral (55,16%) é o Verdejante, que dispõe, dentro de seu território, de uma casa de operação e de bombas que abastecem os domicílios (figura 13).

segundo dados do IBGE, os loteamentos que deveriam receber obras de saneamento somavam, em 2010, 6.059 (seis mil e cinquenta e nove) domicílios, e desses, cerca de 5.141 (cinco mil cento e quarenta e um) não possuiam abastecimento de água por rede geral. Assim, uma vez que o Programa Saneamento Para Todos constitui-se como a primeira iniciativa voltada a ampliação do abastecimento de água desse território, alerta-se que as ligações previstas não abrangem a totalidade dos loteamentos, pois, conforme dados do IBGE, aproximadamente 917 (novecentos e dezessete) domicílios irão permanecer sem abastecimento por rede geral

raw_response.exposure: Implementation of the Programa Saneamento Para Todos by COSANPA (regulated by Resolução CC/FGTS nº 478/2005, IN nº 23/2005, and IN nº 43/2012), specifically its tariff and consumption-block rule (R$ 24.90/month for up to 10 m³, with volumetric surcharges above 10 m³), historical land-occupation regularity/formalization across planned vs. irregular subdivisions, and public-works procurement/contracting governance (Concorrência Pública nº 009/2017, five contract amendments, and a cap of 4,154 planned connections)
raw_response.outcome: Household drinking-water supply source (piped general network coverage of 3.07%–15.55% in informal/regularized subdivisions vs. 55.16% in formal Verdejante; reliance on wells/springs of 44.42%–88.89%), baseline sewerage type, consumption-block exceedance and tariff affordability burden relative to household size (3.68–3.87 residents/household) and per-capita income (R$ 214.10–R$ 363.57 vs. CadÚnico low-income threshold), resident refusal/reliance on informal alternatives, and network connection exclusion (~917 unserved households excluded from the 4,154 planned connections) alongside delayed physical execution
raw_response.population_and_sample: Households and residents in the Águas-Lindas neighborhood straddling Belém and Ananindeua, Pará, Brazil: 9,740 households and 36,362 residents across 6 subdivisions (loteamentos) geoprocessed from 2010 IBGE Census tracts (including 6,059 total households and 5,141 unserved households in the 5 subdivisions targeted for water expansion), 43 monthly COSANPA investment status spreadsheets (Jan 2019–Sep 2022) and procurement contract documents, and 2022 systematic field observations
raw_response.rationale: This Portuguese-language full-text article (matching record metadata R56C569132942) is an empirical mixed-methods case study of household water access in the Águas-Lindas neighborhood (Belém/Ananindeua, Pará, Brazil) under the Programa Saneamento Para Todos. It satisfies all inclusion criteria under both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2: beyond infrastructure expansion, it empirically examines the program's R$ 24.90 / 10 m³ monthly tariff-block and cost-recovery rule against census-tract household sizes and per-capita incomes, maps formal vs. irregular settlement occupation patterns against piped network exclusion, and audits public procurement amendments and connection caps that leave ~917 unserved households excluded from piped water access.
raw_response.study_design: Mixed-methods (quali-quantitative) socio-spatial and documentary case study combining census-tract geoprocessing, administrative procurement/investment document analysis, and systematic field observation
